basic_information.official_title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE APPORTIONMENT OF PARLIAMENTARY DISTRICT REPRESENTATIVE SEATS IN THE BANGSAMORO AUTONOMOUS REGION IN MUSLIM MINDANAO
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or a newspaper of regional circulation in the BARMM
basic_information.title_note: The short title as enacted reads “Bangsamoro Parliamentary Districts Act of 2025”, although Parliament passed it on 12 January 2026 and it was approved on 20 January 2026. Recorded as enacted.

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: The region's third parliamentary district map in 2 years. It keeps the 32 seats and the provincial allocation set in 2025, but revises which municipalities and barangays sit in which district.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: The act states no reason beyond apportioning district representative seats. It re-enacts the map rather than amending the previous one, and repeals anything inconsistent with it.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: Seat counts stay as they were — Basilan 4, Lanao del Sur 9, both Maguindanao provinces 5, Tawi-Tawi 4, Cotabato City 3, Special Geographic Area 2 — but the groupings within them change again, and some population figures are restated.
who_will_be_affected: Every voter in the BARMM, whose district may have changed for the third time
Candidates, whose constituency composition shifts again
Cotabato City residents, whose barangay groupings and stated population are revised
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force from 2026 — 15 days after publication. This is the most recent districting act in the registry.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW, and this is the current map. Same 32 seats as 2025, but the municipalities and barangays inside them have been reshuffled again — check your district.
in_practice: 32 single-member parliamentary districts, on a stated regional population of 4,545,586
Basilan 4 · Lanao del Sur 9 · Maguindanao del Norte 5 · Maguindanao del Sur 5 · Tawi-Tawi 4 · Special Geographic Area 2 · City of Cotabato 3
Sulu holds no parliamentary districts, as under the 2025 act
The apportionment criteria are unchanged: population and geographical area, contiguous compact and adjacent territory, and at least 100,000 people per district
Groupings within provinces are revised — for example, Lanao del Sur's 2nd District now contains Kapai in place of Tagoloan II
Cotabato City's stated total population falls to 359,944, from 383,383 in the 2025 act, with barangay assignments revised

for_specific_groups.Voters: This is the operative map. Check your municipality here rather than in BAA 58 or BAA 77 — groupings changed again even where seat counts did not.
for_specific_groups.Cotabato City residents: Your barangay may sit in a different district from the 2025 act, and the city's stated population is lower by 23,439.
for_specific_groups.Lanao del Sur: Nine districts as before, but the composition of several has changed.
for_specific_groups.Sulu: No districts, as under the 2025 redistricting act. This act contains no transitory provision on the subject.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: The BARMM as constituted under this act.
what_you_can_do: Find your municipality or barangay in this act's district lists — it supersedes the earlier maps
Compare against BAA 77 if you need to know what changed
watch_out_for: This is the third districting map in under 2 years. Anyone relying on an earlier one is working from a superseded list.
The stated regional population differs from the 2025 act by 100 people — 4,545,586 here against 4,545,486 there — with no explanation.
Cotabato City's stated population is 23,439 lower than in the 2025 act.
Unlike the 2025 act, this one carries no transitory provision on Sulu rejoining and no clause on interim representatives for new districts.
The short title dates the act to 2025 although it was passed in January 2026.

key_terms_explained.Apportionment: Distributing the number of seats among areas.
key_terms_explained.Redistricting: Redrawing which places sit inside each district.
key_terms_explained.Single-member district: A district returning exactly one representative.
key_terms_explained.Contiguous, compact and adjacent: The standard that a district should be one connected shape rather than scattered pieces.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Rajab 23, 1447 / 12 January 2026, approved by Chief Minister Abdulraof A. Macacua on 20 January 2026.

benefits.headline: The current, operative parliamentary district map, with every district's population published.

direct_benefits.benefit: A settled and current district for every voter
Published population figures for each district
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Anyone checking whether representation is equitable

indirect_benefits: Retention of the two Special Geographic Area seats introduced in 2025
Retention of the 100,000 minimum population per district
limitations: No stated reason for the revisions.
Population discrepancies against the previous act are unexplained.

for_citizens: None. The act redraws boundaries; it imposes no duty.

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts and creates no offences.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.

where_to_complain.first_stop: Commission on Elections, through the Bangsamoro Electoral Office
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no challenge or complaints procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: A voter in Kapai, Lanao del Sur was in the 3rd District under the 2025 map; under this act Kapai sits in the 2nd District.
A resident of Cotabato City checks their barangay and finds it in a different district from the 2025 act — the city's three districts were recomposed.
A candidate planning a campaign uses this act's lists, since it repeals anything inconsistent with it in the earlier districting laws.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Title: the “Bangsamoro Parliamentary Districts Act of 2025”.
Section 2 — Policy: the Bangsamoro Parliament shall ensure the equitable representation of the inhabitants of the BARMM in the apportionment of parliamentary districts.

Section 3 — Criteria: parliamentary districts are apportioned among the provinces, cities, municipalities and other geographical areas of the BARMM based on population and geographical area; each district shall comprise, as far as practicable, contiguous, compact and adjacent territory and shall have a population of at least 100,000.

Section 4 — Apportions thirty-two single-member parliamentary districts against a stated BARMM population of 4,545,586: Basilan 4 districts (541,947); Lanao del Sur 9 (1,368,137); Maguindanao del Norte 5; Maguindanao del Sur 5; Tawi-Tawi 4; the Special Geographic Area 2 (1st District: Kadayangan, Nabalawag, Pahamuddin, Tugunan; 2nd District: Malidegao, Ligawasan, Old Kaabakan, Kapalawan); and the City of Cotabato 3 (359,944), enumerated barangay by barangay. Sulu holds no districts.
Section 6 — Repeals, amends or modifies all regional laws, rules and regulations inconsistent with the act.
Section 7 — Takes effect 15 days after publication in the Bangsamoro Gazette or a newspaper of regional circulation.

impact.figures_note: Population figures quoted from Section 4: a regional total of 4,545,586, against 4,545,486 in BAA 77 and 4,944,800 in BAA 58.

related_legislation.related_note: The third and most recent parliamentary districting act, after BAA 58 (2024) and BAA 77 (2025). Unlike BAA 77 it does not amend the earlier acts by reference but re-enacts the map and repeals what is inconsistent with it.

implementation_status.note: Read from the enacted text as signed. This is the most recent districting act in the registry and should be treated as the operative map. It omits the transitory provision on Sulu and the interim representative clause found in BAA 77; whether those survive as not inconsistent with this act is not settled by the text.

citizen_questions.a: Yes. It is the most recent of three districting acts — BAA 58 in 2024, BAA 77 in 2025, and this one in January 2026 — and it repeals anything inconsistent with it.

citizen_questions.q: Did the number of seats change?
citizen_questions.a: No. Thirty-two single-member districts, allocated as in the 2025 act: Basilan 4, Lanao del Sur 9, Maguindanao del Norte 5, Maguindanao del Sur 5, Tawi-Tawi 4, Cotabato City 3, and the Special Geographic Area 2.

Which places sit in which district. Groupings were revised within provinces — Lanao del Sur's 2nd District now contains Kapai instead of Tagoloan II, for instance — and Cotabato City's barangay assignments and stated population were reworked.
No. As under the 2025 act, Sulu holds no parliamentary districts. This act contains no transitory provision about the province rejoining.
The short title as enacted reads “Act of 2025”, although Parliament passed it on 12 January 2026. The registry records the title as enacted.
